Ch. 1–4: apply generally
Ch. 5–7: special — supplement or modify 1–4
Ch. 8: communications — independent unless referenced
Ch. 9: tables (mandatory where referenced)
Annexes: informational only

'Shall' / 'shall not' → mandatory
'Shall be permitted' / 'shall not be required' → permissive
Informational notes and annexes → explanatory, not enforceable

Accessible (equipment): reachable, not guarded by locked doors/height
Accessible (wiring): can be removed/exposed without damaging the building
Readily accessible: reach quickly — no climbing, obstacles, or ladders
Visible AND not more than 50 ft (15 m) away

Continuous load: max current expected for 3 hours or more
Ampacity: max current carried continuously without exceeding the temperature rating, under conditions of use
Overcurrent: any current above rated — overload, short circuit, ground fault

Circuits ≤ 100 A or 14–1 AWG: 60°C column (unless equipment marked 75°C)
Circuits > 100 A or larger than 1 AWG: 75°C column
90°C conductors: use the 90°C column only for derating math

0–150 V: 3 ft (all conditions)
151–600 V: Cond. 1 → 3 ft · Cond. 2 → 3½ ft · Cond. 3 → 4 ft
601–1000 V: 3 ft / 4 ft / 5 ft
Cond. 1: insulated/no live parts opposite · Cond. 2: grounded parts opposite · Cond. 3: live parts both sides

front: Working space width, height, dedicated space
back:
Width: 30 in. or equipment width, whichever greater; doors open 90°
Height: 6½ ft or equipment height
Dedicated space: floor to 6 ft above equipment or structural ceiling — no foreign systems

Install listed equipment per its listing/labeling instructions (110.3(B))
Neat and workmanlike manner (110.12); unused openings closed; no damaged equipment

Arc-flash warning on switchboards/panels/MCCs in other than dwellings (110.16)
Field-applied hazard markings durable (110.21(B))
Disconnects marked for purpose unless obvious (110.22)

front: Entrance to working space — 1200 A rule
back:
Equipment ≥ 1200 A and over 6 ft wide: an entrance ≥ 24 in. wide × 6½ ft high at EACH end (or an unobstructed exit / double working space)
Personnel doors within 25 ft: open outward with panic hardware (800 A+)

front: Branch circuit vs feeder vs service conductors
back:
Service conductors: utility point to service disconnect
Feeder: service equipment (or source) to the final branch-circuit OCPD
Branch circuit: final OCPD to the outlets
